# Council round 0 review: intake scorer, manifests, split and guardrails Score: **6/10.** The frozen hashes, exact AST comparison, live network witness and determinism check are solid. But the scorer never penalizes added structure, so a candidate can raise fidelity with false structure and still pass every gate. I'd fix that before the first candidate. **What checks out:** I checked these directly or reproduced them. - All 24 fixture hashes match, and `verify_frozen` passes. - The split is 2 tuning and 1 held-out per format, with 160 expected elements. - A temp-dir run of `generate.py` reproduced all 15 generated fixtures byte for byte. - The DOCX and PPTX image hashes and dimensions match their media parts, including both repeated occurrences. - The `study-pdf` `pixels_sha256` matches the decoded DeviceRGB stream. - The `harbor-pptx` chart strings match `chart1.xml`. ## Findings **High** 1. **Added structure is free.** `score.py:61` only lists leftover elements. `compare()` (128–137) checks `old - new` and never `new - old`. - Trigger: I ran these cases in memory against the scorer. Promoting every paragraph to a heading or duplicating a table scores 1.0 with no loss flagged. - Fix: reject any new heading, list item, table, code or image element compared with baseline unless it matches the manifest. Add negative expectations for body lines in PDF, XLSX and text fixtures. **Medium** 2. **Reading order is not scored.** `generate.py:85-88` places both PDF columns at the same y. If extraction interleaves the columns into one paragraph, the body-text substring checks still pass; I confirmed this in memory. The manifest basis still claims "columns preserve local order". - Fix: add a sequence expectation that requires matched positions to increase in document order. 3. **`nested-docx` can only score 6/6 by duplicating content** (`manifests.json:167` plus the separate inner table). GFM cannot nest a table inside a cell. The no-separator string also depends on the inventory dropping `
`; a converter that separates cell paragraphs with spaces fails. - Fix: choose one representation, or accept alternatives, and define the separator explicitly. 4. **Any error counts as a hostile refusal** (`score.py:231`). If a candidate removes the inflate budget, `hostile-inflate.docx` fails with Timeout and still passes. - Fix: require the same error kind as baseline, and only Invalid or Budget. 5. **Run order is biased** (`score.py:187`). Baseline always runs immediately before final, so every paired difference carries a position bias. - Fix: alternate ABBA per repetition, or randomize with a recorded seed. 6. **The held-out set is weak.** Six of the 8 held-out fixtures are `reserve-*` copies of tuning fixtures: same generator, font sizes, coordinates and merge range. Tuning `island.pptx` is built from the held-out `harbor.pptx` package. All held-out expectations are readable during the climb. - Fix: describe held-out results as a template-variant check only, or write structurally different held-out fixtures. 7. **Sheet-name expectations don't discriminate** (`manifests.json:819`, `879`). The A1 cell repeats the sheet name, and text and table matching draw from separate pools, so one cell satisfies both. Dropping sheet 1's name costs nothing. - Fix: make the sheet name and A1 differ. 8. **The freeze anchors to itself.** Editing `manifests.json` and `frozen.json` together passes `verify_frozen`. The hostile fixture set is a glob, not a frozen list. - Fix: record the `frozen.json` hash in `scorer-review.json`, and check `git diff d8d32c6c` on the frozen paths. 9. **Several guardrails have no tool check.** Nothing checks stock helper source, dependencies (both `Cargo.lock` files, `adapted.Cargo.lock`, `patches/xberg`), AI Off or the size ratio. - Fix: add `git diff --exit-code` receipts and compute the size ratio in a script. 10. **There is no rule for an overall speed decision** (`score.py:220-222`). The scorer makes 64 per-row comparisons but defines no aggregate keep rule, which leaves room to cherry-pick. - Fix: define the aggregate rule in code, plus a per-row slowdown limit. **Low** - `"2"` and `"0"` (`manifests.json:775`, `779`) match any digit left in any block, so chart values are never tied to their categories. - Arm roles come from JSON key order (`score.py:217`). A single-arm run reports all guardrails green. Require exactly `baseline` and `final` keys. - Nothing enforces scoring held-out only once. - Text matching deletes the matched span (`score.py:48`), which can join its neighbours into a new match. Replace it with a sentinel character instead. - `intake_inventory.rs:47` trusts the image hash and size the converter reports. Recompute them from the image bytes. - `island.pptx` and `nested.docx` keep content-type entries for parts that were removed (`generate.py:51`, `62`). - The warm probe never reads stderr (`score.py:91`), so heavy stderr output could hang it. - The README says both temperatures get a warmup run; only warm does. I made no changes. One slip: I ran `python3 generate.py` from `tools/intake-score`, where the script doesn't exist. It failed without writing anything, and `git status` stayed clean. The reproducibility check ran in a temp directory, which I deleted. I didn't score held-out, run the converter, or use providers or the network.
